title: Sub-lemma A: Existence of fixed-degree, A-free 'cancellation invariants' that launder out the unknown generic A

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Goal.** The map $\mathbf F$ must be A-independent and act on the *masked* data $\{\lambda_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}Q^{(\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)}\}$. Since one cannot read $\lambda_c$ off $\lambda_c Q^{(c)}$ without knowing $A$, the entire construction hinges on building, for each pair of cells sharing three of four indices, a *fixed-degree* polynomial contraction $\Phi$ with
$$\Phi(Q^{(\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)})=c\cdot g(A^{(\beta)},A^{(\gamma)},A^{(\delta)})\cdot h_\alpha,$$
so that the *same* $A$-factor $g$ appears in two cells and cancels in the cross-difference
$\Phi(\lambda_{\alpha\cdots})\Phi(\lambda_{\alpha'\cdots'})-\Phi(\lambda_{\alpha\cdots'})\Phi(\lambda_{\alpha'\cdots})$, leaving (up to a known constant) the Segre $2\times2$ minor of $\lambda$.

**What must be proved.** (i) such $\Phi$ exists for each mode; (ii) the shared $A$-factor is generically nonzero; (iii) the resulting list of relations is a valid (degree-bounded, A-free) candidate for the coordinates of $\mathbf F$.

**Why hard.** This is the crux: cancelling the unknown generic $A$ using only $O(1)$-degree, A-free combinations. Use the alternating-core identity $Q^{(\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)}=\mathcal E\times_1A^{(\alpha)}\times_2A^{(\beta)}\times_3A^{(\gamma)}\times_4A^{(\delta)}$ with $\mathcal E$ the $4\times4\times4\times4$ Levi-Civita tensor (verified numerically).
